clues.text: While Moses was on the mountain, Aaron took the people's gold earrings and shaped this idol with an engraving tool.
Moses burned it in the fire, ground it to powder, scattered it on the water, and made Israel drink it.
When the lost son came home, his father told the servants to bring the fattened one and kill it for a feast.
Questioned by Moses, Aaron claimed he threw the people's gold into the fire and this simply came out.
Abraham ran to his herd and chose a tender, choice one to serve the three visitors under the tree.
In John's vision of God's throne, the second of the four living creatures looked like this.
When King Saul was distraught, a woman quickly slaughtered the fattened one at her house and fed him.
